name: Light-wave processor
subtitle: electronics switched by the wave of light itself

effects.effect: lasers can make flashes short enough to freeze electrons moving in atoms

effect: lasers can make flashes short enough to freeze electrons moving in atoms
how: Chips stopped getting faster around 2005 because transistors cannot switch more than a few billion times a second without overheating. Here the electric field of a laser pulse, shaped to within attoseconds, pulls electrons across a tiny gap and pushes them back within a single wave of light, so a switch could flip about a million times faster than today's.
obstacle: Single light-wave switches work in the lab, but wiring billions together and reading them out at that speed is unsolved.
why: A single light-field logic gate was shown in 2022; no processor exists.
real: A single light-field-controlled logic gate in graphene was demonstrated (Nature 2022), but no multi-gate processor or circuit exists.
